texts: good. the denial is scoped to the lighting alone — the lantern stays inside it, while the night and Coraline's apprenticeship, both definite, are kept as standing facts — and the night is recorded as the first one of that apprenticeship.
good. Pell is recorded as a co-walker rather than as a means, the Cliff Path is typed as a path under its own name, and sundown and dawn are kept as the start and end of the walk.
good. the case is typed as a leather case with its 'case' genus and tied to Pell as possessor, and carrying it leaves it unchanged, so it is correctly the thing moved.
good. the glass is recorded as a part of the lantern and as the object the cleaning changes, and the lantern is the same one the rest of the episode uses.
good. same clean shape as the cleaning — the wick is a part of the lantern and the object the trimming changes.
good. the reservoir is a part of the lantern and the mire-essence is recorded as the substance used; 'mire-essence' also gets its 'essence' genus, so a question about essences reaches it.
good. a fresh lighting event on the same lantern, kept distinct from the lighting denied in the first sentence, with Pell as the agent.

bad: 'each step' is read as a universal over steps in general, so the rule says Coraline wrote every step there is; and because nothing in the episode is typed as a step, it can never fire on Pell's cleaning, trimming, filling and lighting — the set you mean is unreachable. The object role inside that rule is wrong as well: writing produces the record, so the notebook entry should count as something the writing creates rather than something merely handled. Name the items instead of quantifying over a kind: "Coraline Ash wrote the cleaning, the trimming, the filling and the lighting in a notebook." — each one then refers back to an event the episode actually narrated. If you want to keep the wording close to the original, "Coraline Ash wrote the steps in a notebook." at least records one asserted writing of a specific set rather than a claim about steps at large.
